claim: You can run Amazon RDS on premises using Amazon RDS on Outposts.
question: Is there an on-premises or hybrid option for Amazon RDS?

values.display: Amazon RDS on Outposts

evidence.quote: Yes, you can run Amazon RDS on premises using Amazon RDS on Outposts.

claim: Billing for a DB instance starts as soon as it is available and continues until the instance terminates, on deletion or instance failure; to stop paying instance hours you must stop or delete it.
question: When does billing for an RDS DB instance start and stop?

values.display: as soon as the DB instance is available
you must stop or delete it

evidence.quote: Billing commences for a DB instance as soon as the DB instance is available. Billing continues until the DB instance terminates, which would occur upon deletion or in the event of an instance failure.
If you no longer wish to be charged for your DB instance, you must stop or delete it to avoid being billed for additional instance hours.

claim: A Multi-AZ DB instance deployment is billed at Multi-AZ pricing; write I/O usage doubles because data is synchronously replicated to the standby, read I/O stays the same, and replication data transfer between primary and standby is not charged.
question: How does a Multi-AZ DB instance deployment change the RDS bill?

values.display: Multi-AZ pricing
Write I/O usage associated with database updates will double
not charged for the data transfer

evidence.quote: If you specify that your DB instance should be a Multi-AZ deployment, you will be billed according to the Multi-AZ pricing posted on the Amazon RDS pricing page.
Write I/O usage associated with database updates will double as Amazon RDS synchronously replicates your data to the standby DB instance. Read I/O usage will remain the same.
Data transfer – You are not charged for the data transfer incurred in replicating data between your primary and standby.

claim: Backup storage is free up to the account's total provisioned database storage in a Region; only backup storage beyond that amount is charged, and the free allowance is per account and per Region.
question: How much RDS backup storage is free?

values.display: Free backup storage is provided up to your account's total provisioned database storage
account-specific and region-specific

evidence.quote: Free backup storage is provided up to your account's total provisioned database storage across the entire region.
Please note that the free backup storage is account-specific and region-specific.

claim: Primary DB storage is in a single Availability Zone, while backup data including transaction logs is replicated across multiple Availability Zones for durability.
question: Do RDS backups survive the loss of one Availability Zone?

values.display: replicated across multiple Availability Zones
located within a single Availability Zone

evidence.quote: The storage provisioned to your DB instance for your primary data is located within a single Availability Zone. When your database is backed up, the backup data (including transactions logs) is geo-redundantly replicated across multiple Availability Zones to provide even greater levels of data durability.

claim: Accounts that sign up for the AWS Free Tier after July 15, 2025 choose a Free Plan or Paid Plan with $100 in credits (plus up to $100 more), valid for up to 12 months; accounts from before that date keep the old offer of up to 750 hours per month of select Single-AZ instances for 12 months.
question: What does the AWS Free Tier give for Amazon RDS today?

values.display: $100 in credits
750 hours per month

qualifiers.scope: AWS Free Tier for Amazon RDS

evidence.quote: If you sign up for AWS Free Tier after July 15, 2025, you can choose between a Free Plan or a Paid Plan for access to RDS. Either plan will offer $100 in credits and up to an additional $100 in credits for activating foundational AWS services. Free Tier credits are valid for up to 12 months.
If you signed up for AWS Free Tier prior to July 15, 2025, you can continue to use RDS for free for up to 12 months on select single-AZ instance databases with up to 750 hours per month.

claim: To increase write availability and protect recent updates against failures, AWS recommends Multi-AZ rather than read replicas: Multi-AZ replication is synchronous, while read replica writes arrive after they happen on the source and lag can vary significantly.
question: Should you use a read replica or Multi-AZ to protect the latest writes against failure?

values.display: we recommend you run your DB instance as a Multi-AZ deployment
this replication “lag” can vary significantly

evidence.quote: If you are looking to use replication to increase database write availability and protect recent database updates against various failure conditions, we recommend you run your DB instance as a Multi-AZ deployment.

With Amazon RDS Read Replicas, which employ supported engines' native, asynchronous replication, database writes occur on a read replica after they have already occurred on the source DB instance, and this replication “lag” can vary significantly.

claim: When a Multi-AZ source fails over, its available read replicas resume replication automatically from the newly promoted primary once failover completes.
question: What happens to read replicas when their Multi-AZ source fails over?

values.display: automatically resume replication once failover has completed

qualifiers.scope: read replicas of a Multi-AZ DB instance deployment

evidence.quote: In the event of Multi-AZ failover, any associated and available read replicas will automatically resume replication once failover has completed (acquiring updates from the newly promoted primary).

claim: RDS for MySQL, MariaDB, PostgreSQL and Oracle let you enable Multi-AZ on read replicas, for disaster recovery and less downtime from engine upgrades.
question: Which engines allow Multi-AZ read replicas?

values.display: enable Multi-AZ configuration on read replicas

evidence.quote: Yes. Amazon RDS for MySQL, MariaDB, PostgreSQL, and Oracle allow you to enable Multi-AZ configuration on read replicas to support disaster recovery and minimize downtime from engine upgrades.

claim: A read replica can fall behind when write I/O on the source exceeds the replica's apply rate (more likely if the replica has less compute), when complex or long-running transactions hold up replication, or because of network partitions or latency.
question: Why does an RDS read replica fall behind its source?

values.display: Complex or long-running transactions
Network partitions or latency

evidence.quote: Write I/O volume to the source DB instance exceeds the rate at which changes can be applied to the read replica (this problem is particularly likely to arise if the compute capacity of a read replica is less than the source DB Instance)
Complex or long-running transactions to the source DB Instance hold up replication to the read replica
Network partitions or latency between the source DB instance and a read replica

claim: For effective replication AWS recommends read replicas with as much or more compute and storage as their source; otherwise replication lag likely increases or the replica can run out of space.
question: What happens if a read replica is smaller than its source?

values.display: as much or more compute and storage resources
replication lag is likely to increase

evidence.quote: For replication to work effectively, we recommend that read replicas have as much or more compute and storage resources as their respective source DB instances. Otherwise replication lag is likely to increase or your read replica may run out of space to store replicated updates.

claim: Billing for a read replica begins when it has been created (status active) and continues at standard DB instance hour rates until you delete it.
question: When does an RDS read replica start and stop costing money?

values.display: begins as soon as the replica has been successfully created
until you issue a command to delete it

evidence.quote: Billing for a read replica begins as soon as the replica has been successfully created (i.e. when the status is listed as “active”). The read replica will continue being billed at standard Amazon RDS DB instance hour rates until you issue a command to delete it.

claim: RDS for MySQL can permit DDL statements on a read replica by setting the read_only parameter to 0 in its DB parameter group; RDS for PostgreSQL does not support DDL on a read replica.
question: Can you add an index directly on an RDS read replica?

values.display: setting the “read_only” parameter to “0.”
does not currently support the execution of DDL SQL statements

qualifiers.scope: RDS for MySQL and RDS for PostgreSQL read replicas

evidence.quote: If you wish to enable operations other than reads for a given read replica, modify the active DB parameter group for the read replica setting the “read_only” parameter to “0.”
Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL does not currently support the execution of DDL SQL statements against a read replica.
